review: The hymn is Ephesians 2 with 1 John 3:2: 1:1–4 is Eph 2:5–6,10 (הֱקִימָנוּ … בְּחַיִּים חֲדָשִׁים, cf. Rom 6:4's חֲדָשׁוּת הַחַיִּים), 2:1–4 is Eph 2:10 with 1 Pet 2:9 (קָרָא … לְאוֹר פֶּלֶא), 3:1–4 is 1 Cor 6:19–20, 4:1–4 is Eph 4:15 with 2 Pet 3:18, 5:1–4 is Heb 13:14, and 6:1–4 is 1 John 3:2–3 almost word for word.

1:2 מֵתִים הָיִינוּ בַּפֶּשַׁע — the Arabic إِذْ كُنَّا أَمْوَاتًا خُطَاه uses a singular 'trespass' like the Greek παράπτωμα of Eph 2:1, so the Hebrew keeps the singular בַּפֶּשַׁע and not the usual plural, because the verse's point is the one condition, not a list of sins.

2:2 נֵלֵךְ בְּעִקְבֵי דוֹדִי — the stanza repeats נֵלֵךְ from 1:3 because the Arabic repeats نَسْلُكُ (1:3) and نَتْبَعُ (2:2); 'following' and 'walking' are then the same motion, which is the stanza's argument, and עִקְבֵי is the biblical 'heel-prints' of Ps 89:52 and Song 1:8.

4:1 נִגְדַּל בְּדַעַת אֵל — the Arabic وَلْنَنْمُ فِي مَعْرِفَةِ الـرَّبِّ splits 'the Lord' across lines ('الـ' / 'ـرَّبِّ'); Hebrew cannot divide a word across lines without breaking the reader, so the break falls at the natural construct boundary and the next line names the Redeemer.

6:4 הוּא יְטַהֵר נַפְשׁוֹ — the Arabic فَنَفْسَهُ يُطَهِّرُ is 1 John 3:3 (כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־לוֹ הַתִּקְוָה הַזֹּאת יְטַהֵר אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ); the Hebrew adds the pronoun הוּא only to fill the line, and keeps יְטַהֵר as the verse's Piel, so purification stays an act and not a state.
